E073-01.notes: Series object of 'had': no public libraries, few paved roads, and literacy rates among the lowest -> parallel noun phrases. A switches to an independent clause in the third slot (faulty parallelism); B participial phrase breaks parallelism and dangles; D wordy/awkward 'of it being'.

E073-02.notes: Subject 'the Works Progress Administration' needs a finite verb. A 'beginning' and B 'having begun' are nonfinite -> fragment; D 'which began' makes a relative clause, still no main verb.

E073-03.notes: Farm horse use is off topic. A: sentence says nothing about hiring women; B: says nothing about 'only practical way'; D: no contradiction.

E073-04.notes: 'steep mountain trails' already conveys up-and-down terrain. A redundant (up and down the mountains); B repeats 'steep'/'steeply'; C redundant 'which were in the mountains'. D concise.

E073-05.notes: Hard conditions set up 'Still, the librarians rarely missed'. B mules not mentioned; C not repeated (S4 doesn't mention ice/mud); D weather supports the librarian focus.

E073-06.notes: Contrast between harsh trails and reliability -> 'Still'. Therefore implies cause; Similarly implies likeness; For example implies illustration.

E073-07.notes: Antecedent 'the riders' is plural -> their. its, his or her, one's all singular/mismatched.

E073-08.notes: No punctuation between verb and agent phrase. A comma splits 'donated' from 'by'; B comma splits verb; D semicolon leaves fragment.

E073-09.notes: Only B names specific contents; A, C, D are vague.

E073-10.notes: Register: A, B, C are informal/overstated ('huge hit', 'totally loved', 'went over really big'). D matches the essay's formal tone.

E073-11.notes: Plural subject 'demands' and past context (1943). A singular 'was'; B present and singular; D present perfect singular and wrong tense.

E073-12.notes: B echoes S1's 'no public libraries'. A, C, D introduce side topics (horses, other WPA projects, librarians' later jobs) with no link to S1.

E073-13.notes: 'these scrapbooks' needs S10, the only mention of scrapbooks; S11 'These homemade collections' still follows. Other positions give no antecedent for 'these scrapbooks'.

E073-14.notes: Essay describes a WPA program meeting a regional need. B no comparison to other states; C travel hardships are only one part; D false, S12 gives the reason it ended.

E073-15.notes: 'but they were made of metal and could hurt anyone' makes a compound predicate. A comma splice; C run-on (fused); D semicolon plus 'and' joining clauses inside a 'but' clause is nonstandard.

E073-16.notes: 'lighter and safer to catch' answers S2's danger of metal tins. A, B, C describe content not present in the phrase.

E073-17.notes: Nonessential appositive needs paired commas. B drops closing comma; C drops opening comma; D semicolon creates fragments.

E073-18.notes: Concise. A, B, D redundant (rename/new name, company already identified as Wham-O in S4). C: 'the company renamed the disc the Frisbee' reads cleanly.

E073-19.notes: Word choice: 'altering' = changing. alternating wrong meaning; altared misspelling/homophone and wrong tense form; alterating not a word.

E073-20.notes: Previous sentence: sales soared; this one: disc still wobbled -> concession 'Even so'. As a result implies sales caused wobbling; For example and Likewise wrong relationships.

E073-21.notes: Plural subject 'ridges'; past narrative (1960s). A and C singular verbs; D participle -> fragment. 'steadied' agrees and fits past context.

E073-22.notes: Plain plural, no possession. A and B add apostrophes; C 'all skills level' scrambles the noun.

flags.note: NO CHANGE is placed at option B rather than A; real ACT items always list NO CHANGE first. Not a correctness issue but a format inconsistency (and a quirk that could confuse students used to the convention).

E073-23.notes: Paragraph covers Ultimate and disc golf, new games built on steadier throws; A also links back to the ridges paragraph. B hula hoop off topic; C too narrow (Ultimate only, and before it's introduced); D casual play is not the topic.

E073-24.notes: 'a team sport in which players may not run' correct. B 'which' leaves no role for the relative pronoun (needs preposition); C 'in that' changes meaning to 'because'; D 'where in' ungrammatical.

E073-25.notes: Most specific/precise. A, B, C vague.

E073-26.notes: C links present-day sports to pie-tin origins. A and D about Wham-O/other companies, not origins; B playing catch on campus is a weak echo but doesn't connect to the disc's origin as pie tins or tie the essay together.

flags.note: Factual nuance: the Frisbie Pie Company is generally reported to have closed in 1958, the same year Wham-O renamed the disc (1958 per S5). 'had closed by then' is roughly defensible but slightly shaky; 'even though the pie company closed soon afterward' or 'the same year' would be safer.

E073-27.notes: 'The name' refers to the Frisbee name borrowed in S6; fits before S7 'Sales soon soared.' After S2 or S4 the name hasn't been given; after S9 it's in the ridges discussion.

E073-28.notes: Morrison, Franscioni, Wham-O founders, Headrick all contribute -> not one inventor. A false (had a partner, and not the Frisbee name); B Headrick is one part; C rules are not the main focus.

E073-29.notes: 'Its' = the first poster in S3 showing the bear pouring water on a campfire; the message matches that image. After S1 no poster yet; after S6 interrupts the cub story; after S9 the slogan is about wildfires generally, not campsites.
